title: The Morning UT Bank's Staff Found the Doors Locked in Accra
conflicts: The collapse is disputed and both sides are attributed: the Bank of Ghana (deeply insolvent, owners failed to recapitalise despite agreed plans, 44% non-performing loans, a potential buyer found it too risky, the shareholders' bailout request 'preposterous') versus Amoabeng (investors had proposals, a supervised restructuring would have cost less than the GH¢2.2 billion closure, the clean-up was haphazard and politically influenced, he had resigned as CEO in 2015; but also 'UT must take the blame first'). Court findings: none on guilt or on the revocation. The first charges were withdrawn in February 2020 and replaced by 42 High Court counts; all accused pleaded not guilty; charges against co-accused Johnson Asiama were withdrawn in January 2025 with the other trials to proceed; in January 2026 Amoabeng said he had been in court for almost eight years, and no verdict was found. Figures: BoG provisional liabilities GH¢850m vs assets GH¢112m; Amoabeng's GH¢800m owed; reports of liquidity support differ (over GH¢1.4bn for both banks; a 3News figure that appears mistyped); only BoG's provisional figures and Amoabeng's GH¢2.2bn are used, attributed.
notes: The slate framed it as Amoabeng watching his bank collapse; he says he had stepped down as UT Bank's chief executive in 2015 and was heading the parent group, which the story states. Prosecution allegations from the charge sheet are left out as unproven. Company field shortened to 'UT Bank' because 'Holdings' matched Shoprite Holdings (Whitey Basson, 2016) in the repeat screen; noted in research_notes. Used all 8 searches on this entry, mostly to establish the 2025-2026 court position.
